question.text: A body <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> has an initial velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. It collides elastically with another body <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> of the same mass which has an initial velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. After the collision, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> moves with a velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi mathvariant="italic">v</mi><mo mathvariant="italic">→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mfenced></math>. The energy of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> after the collision is written as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>10</mn></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>. The value of <math><mi>x</mi></math> is

solution.text:
Using the principle of conservation of linear momentum

0.1×3i^ + 0.1×5j^ = 0.1×4i^+j^ + 0.1×v→

v→=-i^ + j^

KB=12×0.1×v2=110 J

x=1
